meta.label: Client edition 008
meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 0.23% to 25,044.65 on Monday as PSU banks gained; foreign investors bought ₹7,212 crore (provisional); US prices rose 0.4% in October.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Wed 11 Nov: NIFTY 50 ends at 25,044.65 as PSU banks rise; US inflation data lifts yields

brief: On Monday, the last session before Tuesday's Diwali Balipratipada holiday, the NIFTY 50 rose 0.23% to 25,044.65 and the Sensex 0.13% to 81,106.65 after a volatile day (HDFC Sky, IANS).

Nifty Bank gained 1.51% as the Nifty PSU Bank index rose 3.73%, while IT and metal shares fell; the NIFTY Midcap 100 added 0.55% and the Smallcap 100 0.10%, and declining shares outnumbered advancing ones (Kotak Neo, Liquide).
Foreign investors bought a net ₹7,212 crore on Monday and domestic institutions sold ₹7,173 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo). The rupee closed 5 paise firmer at 93.93 per dollar (PTI, provisional).

During the holiday, US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October (BLS), US shares and gold fell, the 10-year Treasury yield moved near 5% and Brent settled at $91.49, its lowest since 31 Aug (AP, Reuters).

outlook.headline: US inflation, crude and India's own price data frame the first session after the holiday

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent settled at $91.49 on Tuesday, its lowest since 31 Aug, after President Trump said he would put off new strikes on Iran and Middle East shipments neared prewar levels (Reuters, Rigzone). India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Foreign flows
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹53,172 crore in the cash market from 1 to 9 Nov while domestic institutions sold ₹32,069 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo). Foreign flows feed into large-cap share prices and the rupee; provisional figures can be revised.

drivers.title: Inflation in India
drivers.text: Retail inflation was 5.54% in September (provisional), with food prices up 7.74% (Business Standard). ICRA's Aditi Nayar expects October's reading at 6.1% (NewsBytes). Inflation readings shape rate expectations, which reach bond yields and loan rates.

drivers.title: The rupee and bonds
drivers.text: The rupee firmed 5 paise on Monday on easing crude and foreign inflows, PTI reported, while the 10-year yield rose to 7.17% as investors took profits after a rally (Trading Economics). Bond prices rise when yields fall.

global_cues.title: US inflation and the Fed
global_cues.text: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October and core prices 0.3% (BLS). After the data, CME FedWatch showed a December Fed rate rise fully priced (Seoul Economic Daily), and Fed Governor Waller said he would back at least a quarter-point rise (Reuters). Higher US rates can weigh on foreign flows into Indian shares and bonds.

global_cues.title: US yields and the dollar
global_cues.text: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 10 basis points to near 5% on Tuesday and the dollar index edged higher (Trading Economics). A firmer dollar tends to weigh on the rupee and other emerging-market currencies.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: On Tuesday, while India was shut, Japan's Nikkei rose 2.9% and Korea's Kospi 4.4% (AP). On Wednesday morning the Kospi opened lower, then turned higher, Aju Press reported.

events.title: India inflation
events.text: October retail inflation is due; September's provisional reading was 5.54% (Business Standard).

events.text: Weekly jobless claims on Thursday and October producer prices on Friday (Kiplinger).

events.text: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee meets (Angel One, citing the RBI calendar).

global.headline: US shares fell on Tuesday after hotter inflation data; Japanese and Korean shares rose
global.note: Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose about 0.4% on Tuesday (Reuters). Korea's Kospi opened about 0.6% lower on Wednesday, then turned higher by mid-morning (Aju Press).

us.title: The session
us.text: US shares fell on Tuesday after October consumer prices rose more than expected (TheStreet). Regan Capital's Skyler Weinand, quoted by TheStreet, described a move out of AI-linked shares into defensive sectors such as healthcare.

us.title: Inflation
us.text: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October and core prices 0.3%; the BLS published no 12-month rate for the headline index because October 2025 survey data were not collected.

us.title: Shares and rates
us.text: Nvidia fell 5.47% and at one point slipped to third by market value (Seoul Economic Daily). The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 10 basis points to 4.99% (Trading Economics).

events.title: December Fed rate rise priced in
events.text: After the inflation data, CME FedWatch showed a quarter-point rise at the 8 to 9 Dec meeting fully priced, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan backed at least two quarter-point rises (Seoul Economic Daily). The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: US puts off new strikes on Iran
events.text: President Trump said he would put off new strikes after appeals from regional countries, including Qatar's prime minister (Reuters). The channel to India: crude prices and the import bill.

events.title: Gulf oil supply
events.text: Persian Gulf exports have grown and Middle East shipments are near prewar levels; Capital Economics' Hamad Hussain linked the price fall mainly to hopes of a diplomatic end to the war (Rigzone). The channel to India: oil supply and inflation.

commentary.text: Gold and silver fell on Tuesday after the hotter US inflation reading lifted bets on a December Fed rate rise and strengthened the dollar, The Nation reported.
Marex analyst Edward Meir called the slightly hotter inflation figures a short-term negative for gold (The Nation).
World Gold Council data showed China's central bank bought 25.8 tonnes of gold in October, its largest monthly addition in three years (Trading Economics).

highlights.text: Among equity categories, small cap funds took ₹9,039 crore net, mid cap ₹7,835 crore, flexi cap ₹6,702 crore and multi cap ₹3,860 crore; ELSS funds saw a net outflow of ₹662 crore.
Debt funds saw net outflows of ₹1,83,156 crore, which AMFI linked to companies' cash needs ahead of advance tax payments; liquid funds accounted for ₹95,743 crore.
Multi asset allocation funds took ₹3,667 crore, their 61st month in a row of inflows; gold ETFs took ₹4,451 crore and silver ETFs ₹1,974 crore.
Investors added about 27.13 lakh folios in September, taking the total to 28.62 crore.

fund_news.text: HDFC, ICICI Prudential, Aditya Birla Sun Life and Franklin Templeton mutual funds revised the riskometer levels of some schemes, most based on their end-October portfolios, Upstox News reported; some levels went up and some down.

nfo_summary.text: Two new fund offers on Cafemutual's 5 November list remain open on 11 November by their closing dates: a debt fixed maturity plan closing on 17 November and a sectoral index ETF closing on 13 November. Each scheme's category, riskometer level and terms are in its scheme information document. This list is reported for information only and is not a recommendation.

regulatory.text: From 1 April 2027, a mutual fund scheme may net the cash it pays and receives for outright cash-market trades within the scheme; securities still settle trade by trade and netting across schemes is not allowed.
SEBI's Mutual Funds (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026 replace the separate mutual fund advertisement code with the common code for intermediaries, from the 180th day after publication.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, a multi cap fund must keep at least 75% of its assets in equity and equity-related instruments, with at least 25% each in large cap, mid cap and small cap companies. With at least a quarter in each size band, a fixed part of the portfolio always sits in mid and small companies, whose share prices tend to swing more than those of large companies. Each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: Why a scheme's riskometer can change
paragraphs: Every mutual fund scheme shows a riskometer, a dial that places its risk on a scale; the levels named in last week's revisions ran from Low to Very High.
The level follows what the scheme holds. On 6 and 7 November several fund houses revised levels, most based on their end-October portfolios, moving some schemes up and some down (Upstox News).
A change in level does not mean a scheme has changed its category or objective. The latest level, and the reasons for it, are in the fund house's own documents.
